Methods
Cell culture, neuronal differentiation and cell transfection
Neural stem cells, Cor3–1 were grown in Complete media (DMEM/HAM’S-F12 (Sigma, D8437), 1.45% Glucose (Sigma,
G28644
), 1 × MEM-NEAA (Gibco, 11140-035), 100 units/ml penicillin and 100 μg/ml streptomycin (Gibco, 15140-122), 0.16% BSA (Gibco, 15260-037), 0.1 mM β-Mercapto-ethanol (Gibco 31350-010), 1% B-27 supplement (Gibco, 17504-044) and 0.5% N2 supplement (Gibco, 17502-048)). Before changing the medium or passaging the cells, 10 ng/ml mouse EGF (Peprotech, 315-09), 10 ng/ml human FGF (R&D systems, 233-FB) and 1 μg/ml Laminin (Sigma, L2020-1MG) were added to the required volume of Complete media. For neuronal differentiation, 24 hours after seeding, cells were transferred into a priming medium Euromed-N (Euroclone) supplemented with 1% B-27 without vitamin A (Gibco, 12587010), 0.5% N2 and 10 ng/ml human FGF for 3 days. Cells were then transferred into a differentiation medium (1:3 ratio DMEM/HAM’S-F12:Neurobasal (Gibco, 21103-049) supplemented with 1% B-27 without vitamin A, 0.5% N2, 10 ng/ml human FGF, 20 ng/ml BDNF (R&D systems, 248-BD) and 1μg/ml Laminin for 3 days followed by a change of medium every 3 days with reduction of the FGF concentration by half to zero and a constant concentration of BDNF at 30 ng/ml.
Neural stem cells (Floxed-Huwe1-RYFP) used for Huwe1 knock-out were described in King
et al
.
32
and in Urban
et al
., 2017
11
and maintained as described above. Transduction of CRE recombinase was performed with the adenovirus CMV-CRE (Vector Biolabs, 1045 N) at a MOI of 100. Empty adenovirus (CMV-null) was used as control at the same MOI.
P19 cells were maintained in MEM-α (Gibco, 41061-029) supplemented with 10% FBS and 100 units/ml penicillin and 100 μg/ml streptomycin. For differentiation, cells were transferred into Neurobasal medium supplemented with penicillin/streptomycin, 1% B-27 without vitamin A, 1 × GlutaMAX (Thermo, 35050061) and 1μg/ml Laminin. Differentiation medium was changed every 24 hours if required. P19 cells were transfected at 80% confluence with Lipofectamine 2000 (Invitrogen, 11668-027) in proliferation medium following the manufacturer’s instructions with a 1:2 ratio (DNA:Lipofectamine). A list of plasmids is provided in Table
S2
in supplementary information.
Quantitative Real-Time PCR
Total RNA was extracted from cells using the RNeasy kit (Qiagen). Template cDNAs were synthesised using the QuantiTect Reverse Transcription Kit (Qiagen), and qRT-PCR was performed using QuantiFast SYBR Green Master Mix (Qiagen) in a Lightcycler 480 PCR system (Roche). EiF1α was used as housekeeping gene to normalise each qPCR target and the values were calculated as fold increase to proliferation samples. Thermal cycling conditions: 95 °C for 5 mins, then 40 cycles of 95 °C for 10 seconds, 60 °C for 10 seconds and 72 °C for 30 seconds. The primer sequences are provided in Table
S1
in supplementary information. Data are presented as means ± SEM of normalised values from at least three independent experiments.
Western blotting
Western blots were either performed from total cell lysates obtained by lysing cells directly with RIPA buffer (Sigma-Aldrich) complemented with protease inhibitor cocktail (cOmplete, Roche) or from fractionated lysates (see below). Proteins concentration was determined using BCA protein assay kit (Thermo). SDS-PAGE electrophoresis was carried out in 10% pre-cast polyacrylamide gels (Novex) in MOPS buffer. After transfer onto nitrocellulose, membranes were blocked for 1hr with 10% non-fat milk in TBS-0.1% Tween solution and probed overnight with primary antibody: Ascl1 (1:300, hybridoma supernatant, gift from David Anderson and François Guillemot), Histone H3 (1:10,000, Abcam, ab1791) and α-Tubulin (1:10,000, Abcam, ab7291), LaminB (1:500, Santa Cruz, sc-6216) and Huwe1 (1:1,000, Bethyl Laboratories, A300-486A). Mouse secondary (goat anti-mouse HRP 1:10,000, Millipore, 71045-3) or rabbit secondary (1:5,000, Rabbit IgG HRP linked, GE Healthcare, NA934V) antibodies were used for detection in 5% milk in TBS-0.1% Tween solution for 1 hour. Membranes were developed using ECL Prime (GE Healthcare, RPN2232) for Ascl1 or ECL detection reagents (GE Healthcare, RPN2106) for the other antibodies. All western blots were performed at least in triplicate.
Cellular Fractionation
Cor3–1 cells were seeded at 1.5 × 10
6
in 10 cm dishes and P19 were seeded at 1.0 × 10
6
in 10 cm dishes. P19 were transfected with 3 μg of Ascl1 plasmid constructs (Supplementary Table
S2
). Cells were washed once with room temperature PBS and scraped into 1 ml PBS. Cells were pelleted at 1,200 rpm in an eppendorf tube at 4 °C for 3 min. Pellets were covered with 5 volumes of ice-cold E1 buffer (50 mM Hepes-KOH pH 7.5, 140 mM NaCl, 1 mM EDTA pH8.0, 10% glycerol, 0.5% NP-40, 0.25% triton X-100, 1 mM DTT) complemented with 1 × protease inhibitor cocktail and were gently pipetted up and down (5 times) before centrifugation at 3,400 rpm at 4 °C for 2 min. The supernatant was collected in a fresh tube (cytoplasm fraction) and the pellet was resuspended by gentle pipetting in the same volume of E1 buffer and centrifuged as before. The supernatant was discarded and the pellet was resuspended by gentle pipetting in the same volume of E1 and left for 10 min on ice. After centrifugation at 3,400 rpm at 4 °C for 2 min, the supernatant was discarded and the pellet was resuspended by gentle pipetting in 2 volumes of ice-cold E2 buffer (10 mM Tris-HCl pH8.0, 200 mM NaCl, 1 mM EDTA pH8.0, 0.5 mM EGTA pH8.0) complemented with 1 × protease inhibitor cocktail and centrifuged at 3,400 rpm at 4 °C for 2 min. The supernatant was collected in a fresh tube (nucleus fraction) and the pellet was resupsended in the same volume of E2 and centrifuged as before. The supernatant was discarded and the pellet was resuspended in the same volume of E2 and left for 10 min on ice. After centrifugation at 3,400 rpm at 4 °C for 2 min, the supernatant was discarded and the pellet was resuspended in ice-cold E3 buffer (500 mM Tris-HCl, 500 mM NaCl) complemented with 1 × protease inhibitor cocktail by gentle pipetting in the same volume used for E1. The solution (chromatin fraction) was sonicated in a Bioruptor (Diagenode) for 5 min on setting H, 30 sec ON/30 sec OFF for western blot analysis or was digested with Benzonase (1:1,000, Novagen, 70664-3) for TUBEs pull down. All fractions were centrifuged at 13,000 rpm at 4 °C for 10 min and protein concentration was determined using BCA protein assay kit.
Agarose-TUBEs pull down
15 μl of 50% Agarose-TUBEs (LifeSensors, UM401) were used to pull down between 350 μg and 450 μg of ubiquitylated proteins from the cytoplasm and chromatin fractions in 500 μl final volume of respective buffers. Incubation was performed for 1 hour at 4 °C on a rocker platform. Agarose-TUBEs were collected by centrifugation at 1,000 × g at 4 °C for 5 min. The supernatant was collected in a fresh tube (unbound fraction). Agarose-TUBEs were washed 3 times following the manufacturer’s instructions and were boiled in reducing sample buffer (25 μl) for 5 min, centrifuged at maximum speed in a top bench centrifuge for 1 min and eluted samples were loaded onto gels (Bound fraction: 15 μl for Ascl1 and 5 μl for loading controls) alongside 5 μg of proteins from the unbound fraction and 5 μg from fractionated lysates (Input).
Protein Stability Assay
Cor3-1 cells or transfected P19 cells (2 μg Ascl1 plasmid DNA in 6 cm dishes) were treated with 10 μg/ml cycloheximide (Sigma-Aldrich, C4859). At define time points, cells were harvested with RIPA lysis buffer (Sigma-Aldrich, R0278) or fractioned. Equal amount of each whole cell lysate or fractionated lysate was separated on SDS-PAGE and immmunoblotted with mouse anti-Ascl1 and mouse anti-α-Tubulin (1:10,000, Abcam). Protein levels were quantified with FiJi software. Half-lives were calculated using a nonlinear regression analysis (One phase decay, Prism).
Immunocytochemistry
Cor3-1 or P19 cells were plated onto ECM-coated (Sigma, E1270) 24-well plate (25,000 cells per well). At indicated time, cells were fixed in 4% paraformaldehyde for 10 min at room temperature. Cells were then washed twice in PBS and permeabilised in 0.2% Triton X-100 PBS for 10 min at room temperature. Blocking was performed in PBS with 3% BSA for 60 min at room temperature. Anti-Ascl1 primary antibody (Abcam, ab74065) was used at 5 μg/ml final concentration in PBS with 2% FBS and 0.02% Triton X-100 overnight at 4 °C without rocking. The next day, cells were washed 3 times in 0.02% Triton X-100 PBS for 5 mins and incubate with secondary antibody (Alexa488 goat anti-rabbit IgG, Life Technologies) diluted 1:500 in PBS with 2% FBS and 0.02% Triton X-100 for 1 hour at room temperature in the dark. Cells were next washed 3 times in 0.02% Triton X-100 PBS for 5 mins and incubated in 4′,6-diamidino-2-phenylindole (DAPI, 1:10,000) in PBS for 20 min at room temperature in the dark. After 2 washes in PBS, fluorescence labelling was visualised with Axio Scan (Zeiss).
Gene Reporter Assay
P19 cells were plated into 48-well plates (75,000 cells per well) and transfected the day after with 100 ng ΔM short-Luciferase (Supplementary Table
S2
), 50 ng pRL-TK (Renilla, Promega) and 100 ng Ascl1 using Lipofectamine 2000 in proliferation media. One set of cells was harvested the day after (proliferation samples) with the Dual-Luciferase Reporter Assay System (Promega, E1910) while the other set of cells was transferred into differentiation media and harvested 24 hours later. Luciferase assay was performed following the manufacturer’s instructions (Promega) using a Tecan Infinite 200Pro microplate reader. Values for Luciferase were normalised to Renilla-Luciferase values and data are presented as means ± SEM of duplicate and experiments were repeated three times.
Data availability
All data generated or analysed during this study are included in this published article (and its Supplementary Information files).

steps.step_text: Grow Cor3–1 neural stem cells in Complete media.
steps.step_rationale: Cor3–1 neural stem cells require specific media conditions for proper growth and maintenance.
steps.span_chunk: Neural stem cells, Cor3–1 were grown in Complete media (DMEM/HAM’S-F12 (Sigma, D8437), 1.45% Glucose (Sigma, G28644 ), 1 × MEM-NEAA (Gibco, 11140-035), 100 units/ml penicillin and 100 μg/ml streptomycin (Gibco, 15140-122), 0.16% BSA (Gibco, 15260-037), 0.1 mM β-Mercapto-ethanol (Gibco 31350-010), 1% B-27 supplement (Gibco, 17504-044) and 0.5% N2 supplement (Gibco, 17502-048)).

steps.step_text: Supplement Complete media with growth factors before changing the medium or passaging the cells.
steps.step_rationale: Growth factors are necessary to stimulate cell proliferation and health during maintenance and before subculturing.
steps.span_chunk: Before changing the medium or passaging the cells, 10 ng/ml mouse EGF (Peprotech, 315-09), 10 ng/ml human FGF (R&D systems, 233-FB) and 1 μg/ml Laminin (Sigma, L2020-1MG) were added to the required volume of Complete media.

steps.step_text: Maintain P19 cells in MEM-α supplemented with FBS and antibiotics.
steps.step_rationale: P19 cells require specific media conditions for proper growth and maintenance, including a basal medium, serum, and antibiotics to prevent contamination.
steps.span_chunk: P19 cells were maintained in MEM-α (Gibco, 41061-029) supplemented with 10% FBS and 100 units/ml penicillin and 100 μg/ml streptomycin.

steps.step_text: Transfer the seeded neural stem cells into priming medium 24 hours after seeding.
steps.step_rationale: The cells need to be primed before they can be differentiated into neurons.
steps.span_chunk: For neuronal differentiation, 24 hours after seeding, cells were transferred into a priming medium...
materials: Supplements for priming medium (1% B-27 without vitamin A, 0.5% N2, 10 ng/ml human FGF)

steps.step_text: Maintain the cells in the priming medium for 3 days.
steps.step_rationale: A specific duration in the priming medium is necessary to prepare the cells for differentiation.
steps.span_chunk: For neuronal differentiation, 24 hours after seeding, cells were transferred into a priming medium... supplemented with 1% B-27 without vitamin A, 0.5% N2 and 10 ng/ml human FGF for 3 days.

steps.step_text: Transfer the cells into differentiation medium after the priming period.
steps.step_rationale: The cells are now ready to be differentiated into neurons using a specific differentiation medium.
steps.span_chunk: Cells were then transferred into a differentiation medium...
materials: Supplements for differentiation medium (1% B-27 without vitamin A, 0.5% N2, 10 ng/ml human FGF, 20 ng/ml BDNF, 1μg/ml Laminin)

steps.step_text: Change the differentiation medium every 3 days, reducing the FGF concentration by half each time until it reaches zero, while maintaining a constant concentration of BDNF at 30 ng/ml.
steps.step_rationale: Regular medium changes and adjustments in growth factor concentrations are necessary to support the differentiation process and maturation of neurons.
steps.span_chunk: followed by a change of medium every 3 days with reduction of the FGF concentration by half to zero and a constant concentration of BDNF at 30 ng/ml.
parameters: FGF concentration reduction (by half each time until zero)

steps.step_text: Grow P19 cells in MEM-α medium supplemented with 10% FBS and 100 units/ml penicillin and 100 μg/ml streptomycin until they reach 80% confluence.
steps.step_rationale: The cells need to be at the right confluence to ensure optimal transfection efficiency.
steps.span_chunk: P19 cells were maintained in MEM-α (Gibco, 41061-029) supplemented with 10% FBS and 100 units/ml penicillin and 100 μg/ml streptomycin.

steps.step_text: Prepare the transfection mixture by diluting the plasmid DNA and Lipofectamine 2000 in the proliferation medium at a 1:2 ratio (DNA:Lipofectamine).
steps.step_rationale: The transfection mixture needs to be prepared according to the manufacturer's instructions for optimal transfection.
steps.span_chunk: P19 cells were transfected at 80% confluence with Lipofectamine 2000 (Invitrogen, 11668-027) in proliferation medium following the manufacturer’s instructions with a 1:2 ratio (DNA:Lipofectamine).

steps.step_text: Transfect the P19 cells with the prepared mixture when they are at 80% confluence, following the manufacturer's instructions for Lipofectamine 2000.
steps.step_rationale: Transfection should be carried out at the right confluence and using the correct procedure to introduce the DNA into the cells efficiently.
steps.span_chunk: P19 cells were transfected at 80% confluence with Lipofectamine 2000 (Invitrogen, 11668-027) in proliferation medium following the manufacturer’s instructions with a 1:2 ratio (DNA:Lipofectamine).

steps.step_text: Extract total RNA from cells using the RNeasy kit (Qiagen).
steps.step_rationale: The initial step in quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) is to extract RNA from cells, which will be used to synthesize cDNA.
steps.span_chunk: Total RNA was extracted from cells using the RNeasy kit (Qiagen).

steps.step_text: Synthesize template cDNAs using the QuantiTect Reverse Transcription Kit (Qiagen).
steps.step_rationale: Following RNA extraction, the RNA is reverse transcribed to cDNA, which serves as a template for the PCR reaction.
steps.span_chunk: Template cDNAs were synthesised using the QuantiTect Reverse Transcription Kit (Qiagen),

steps.step_text: Perform qRT-PCR using QuantiFast SYBR Green Master Mix (Qiagen) in a Lightcycler 480 PCR system (Roche).
steps.step_rationale: The cDNA is then used to perform qRT-PCR, which quantifies gene expression levels. The SYBR Green dye is used for detection of the amplified DNA.
steps.span_chunk: qRT-PCR was performed using QuantiFast SYBR Green Master Mix (Qiagen) in a Lightcycler 480 PCR system (Roche).

steps.step_text: Obtain total cell lysates by lysing cells directly with RIPA buffer complemented with protease inhibitor cocktail.
steps.step_rationale: To prepare the sample for Western blotting, cells need to be lysed to release proteins.
steps.span_chunk: Western blots were either performed from total cell lysates obtained by lysing cells directly with RIPA buffer (Sigma-Aldrich) complemented with protease inhibitor cocktail (cOmplete, Roche)

steps.step_text: Determine the protein concentration using the BCA protein assay kit.
steps.step_rationale: Quantifying the protein concentration is essential to load equal amounts of protein onto the gel for separation.
steps.span_chunk: Proteins concentration was determined using BCA protein assay kit (Thermo).

steps.step_text: Carry out SDS-PAGE electrophoresis using 10% pre-cast polyacrylamide gels in MOPS buffer.
steps.step_rationale: SDS-PAGE is used to separate proteins based on their molecular weight.
steps.span_chunk: SDS-PAGE electrophoresis was carried out in 10% pre-cast polyacrylamide gels (Novex) in MOPS buffer.

steps.step_text: Transfer the separated proteins onto nitrocellulose membranes.
steps.step_rationale: Proteins need to be transferred from the gel to a membrane for subsequent antibody probing.
steps.span_chunk: After transfer onto nitrocellulose,

steps.step_text: Block the membranes for 1 hour with 10% non-fat milk in TBS-0.1% Tween solution.
steps.step_rationale: Blocking non-specific binding sites on the membrane is crucial to reduce background noise in the detection.
steps.span_chunk: membranes were blocked for 1hr with 10% non-fat milk in TBS-0.1% Tween solution

steps.step_text: Probe the membranes overnight with primary antibodies specific to the proteins of interest.
steps.step_rationale: Primary antibodies bind to the target proteins, allowing for their detection.
steps.span_chunk: and probed overnight with primary antibody

steps.step_text: Develop the membranes using ECL Prime for Ascl1 or ECL detection reagents for the other antibodies.
steps.step_rationale: Chemiluminescent detection reagents are used to visualize the proteins bound by the primary antibodies.
steps.span_chunk: Membranes were developed using ECL Prime (GE Healthcare, RPN2232) for Ascl1 or ECL detection reagents (GE Healthcare, RPN2106) for the other antibodies.

steps.step_text: Wash cells once with room temperature PBS and scrape into 1 ml PBS.
steps.step_rationale: To remove any residual media and to collect the cells for fractionation.
steps.span_chunk: Cells were washed once with room temperature PBS and scraped into 1 ml PBS.

steps.step_text: Pellet cells by centrifugation at 1,200 rpm at 4°C for 3 minutes.
steps.step_rationale: To separate the cells from the PBS solution.
steps.span_chunk: Cells were pelleted at 1,200 rpm in an eppendorf tube at 4°C for 3 min.

steps.step_text: Resuspend the cell pellet in 5 volumes of ice-cold E1 buffer complemented with 1x protease inhibitor cocktail and pipette gently up and down 5 times.
steps.step_rationale: To lyse the cells and release the cytoplasmic fraction while preserving protein integrity with protease inhibitors.
steps.span_chunk: Pellets were covered with 5 volumes of ice-cold E1 buffer (50 mM Hepes-KOH pH 7.5, 140 mM NaCl, 1 mM EDTA pH8.0, 10% glycerol, 0.5% NP-40, 0.25% triton X-100, 1 mM DTT) complemented with 1x protease inhibitor cocktail and were gently pipetted up and down (5 times).

steps.step_text: Centrifuge at 3,400 rpm at 4°C for 2 minutes and collect the supernatant in a fresh tube (cytoplasm fraction).
steps.step_rationale: To separate the cytoplasmic fraction from the nuclear and chromatin fractions.
steps.span_chunk: Before centrifugation at 3,400 rpm at 4°C for 2 min. The supernatant was collected in a fresh tube (cytoplasm fraction).

steps.step_text: Resuspend the remaining pellet in the same volume of E1 buffer, centrifuge as before, and discard the supernatant.
steps.step_rationale: To wash the pellet and remove any remaining cytoplasmic content.
steps.span_chunk: The pellet was resuspended by gentle pipetting in the same volume of E1 buffer and centrifuged as before. The supernatant was discarded.

steps.step_text: Resuspend the pellet in the same volume of E2 buffer complemented with 1x protease inhibitor cocktail, leave for 10 minutes on ice, centrifuge, and collect the supernatant in a fresh tube (nucleus fraction).
steps.step_rationale: To extract the nuclear fraction while maintaining protein integrity.
steps.span_chunk: The pellet was resuspended by gentle pipetting in the same volume of E2 buffer (10 mM Tris-HCl pH8.0, 200 mM NaCl, 1 mM EDTA pH8.0, 0.5 mM EGTA pH8.0) complemented with 1x protease inhibitor cocktail and left for 10 min on ice. After centrifugation at 3,400 rpm at 4°C for 2 min, the supernatant was collected in a fresh tube (nucleus fraction).

steps.step_text: Resuspend the remaining pellet in ice-cold E3 buffer complemented with 1x protease inhibitor cocktail in the same volume used for E1, sonicate for 5 minutes on setting H, 30 seconds ON/30 seconds OFF, and centrifuge at 13,000 rpm at 4°C for 10 minutes to obtain the chromatin fraction.
steps.step_rationale: To isolate the chromatin fraction and shear the DNA to reduce viscosity.
steps.span_chunk: The pellet was resuspended in ice-cold E3 buffer (500 mM Tris-HCl, 500 mM NaCl) complemented with 1x protease inhibitor cocktail by gentle pipetting in the same volume used for E1. The solution (chromatin fraction) was sonicated in a Bioruptor (Diagenode) for 5 min on setting H, 30 sec ON/30 sec OFF.
parameters: Sonication: 5 minutes, H setting, 30 sec ON/30 sec OFF

steps.step_text: Determine the protein concentration of all fractions using BCA protein assay kit.
steps.step_rationale: To quantify the amount of protein present in each fraction for downstream analysis.
steps.span_chunk: All fractions were centrifuged at 13,000 rpm at 4°C for 10 min and protein concentration was determined using BCA protein assay kit.

steps.step_text: Prepare 15 μl of 50% Agarose-TUBEs for the pull-down assay.
steps.step_rationale: The Agarose-TUBEs are used as a medium to bind and pull down ubiquitylated proteins from the cell fractions.
steps.span_chunk: 15 μl of 50% Agarose-TUBEs (LifeSensors, UM401) were used to pull down between 350 μg and 450 μg of ubiquitylated proteins from the cytoplasm and chromatin fractions

steps.step_text: Incubate the Agarose-TUBEs with 350 μg to 450 μg of ubiquitylated proteins from cytoplasm and chromatin fractions in a final volume of 500 μl of respective buffers.
steps.step_rationale: The ubiquitylated proteins from the cell fractions are incubated with Agarose-TUBEs to allow for binding and pull-down.
steps.span_chunk: 15 μl of 50% Agarose-TUBEs (LifeSensors, UM401) were used to pull down between 350 μg and 450 μg of ubiquitylated proteins from the cytoplasm and chromatin fractions in 500 μl final volume of respective buffers.
materials: Ubiquitylated proteins from cytoplasm and chromatin fractions

steps.step_text: Perform the incubation for 1 hour at 4°C on a rocker platform.
steps.step_rationale: Incubation at 4°C on a rocker platform ensures proper mixing and binding of ubiquitylated proteins to Agarose-TUBEs.
steps.span_chunk: Incubation was performed for 1 hour at 4°C on a rocker platform.

steps.step_text: Collect the Agarose-TUBEs by centrifugation at 1,000 x g at 4°C for 5 minutes.
steps.step_rationale: Centrifugation is used to separate the Agarose-TUBEs with bound proteins from the unbound fraction.
steps.span_chunk: Agarose-TUBEs were collected by centrifugation at 1,000 x g at 4°C for 5 minutes.

steps.step_text: Wash the Agarose-TUBEs three times as per the manufacturer's instructions.
steps.step_rationale: Washing the Agarose-TUBEs removes non-specifically bound proteins and contaminants.
steps.span_chunk: Agarose-TUBEs were washed 3 times following the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.step_text: Boil the Agarose-TUBEs in reducing sample buffer for 5 minutes.
steps.step_rationale: Boiling in reducing sample buffer elutes the bound proteins from the Agarose-TUBEs and prepares them for SDS-PAGE analysis.
steps.span_chunk: Agarose-TUBEs were boiled in reducing sample buffer for 5 minutes.

steps.step_text: Centrifuge the boiled Agarose-TUBEs at maximum speed in a top bench centrifuge for 1 minute.
steps.step_rationale: Centrifugation after boiling ensures that the eluted proteins are collected in the supernatant and separated from the Agarose-TUBEs.
steps.span_chunk: Centrifuged at maximum speed in a top bench centrifuge for 1 minute.

steps.step_text: Load the eluted samples onto gels for analysis.
steps.step_rationale: Loading the eluted samples onto gels allows for the analysis of the ubiquitylated proteins by SDS-PAGE.
steps.span_chunk: Eluted samples were loaded onto gels.

steps.step_text: Treat Cor3-1 cells or transfected P19 cells with 10 μg/ml cycloheximide.
steps.step_rationale: Cycloheximide is used to inhibit protein synthesis, allowing for the assessment of protein degradation over time.
steps.span_chunk: Cor3-1 cells or transfected P19 cells... were treated with 10 μg/ml cycloheximide...

steps.step_text: Harvest cells at defined time points after treatment with cycloheximide.
steps.step_rationale: Harvesting cells at specific time intervals is necessary to measure the rate of protein degradation and calculate half-lives.
steps.span_chunk: At define time points, cells were harvested...

steps.step_text: Prepare equal amounts of each whole cell lysate or fractionated lysate for analysis.
steps.step_rationale: Ensuring equal amounts of lysate allows for accurate comparison of protein levels between samples.
steps.span_chunk: Equal amount of each whole cell lysate or fractionated lysate was separated on SDS-PAGE...

steps.step_text: Separate the lysates on SDS-PAGE and transfer them to a membrane for immunoblotting.
steps.step_rationale: SDS-PAGE separates proteins by size, and immunoblotting allows for the detection of specific proteins using antibodies.
steps.span_chunk: ...was separated on SDS-PAGE and immmunoblotted...

steps.step_text: Quantify the protein levels using FiJi software.
steps.step_rationale: Quantification of protein bands is necessary to determine the amount of protein present at each time point.
steps.span_chunk: Protein levels were quantified with FiJi software.

steps.step_text: Calculate the half-lives of the proteins using nonlinear regression analysis (One phase decay, Prism).
steps.step_rationale: The half-life calculation allows for the determination of the stability of the protein over time.
steps.span_chunk: Half-lives were calculated using a nonlinear regression analysis (One phase decay, Prism).

steps.step_text: Fix the cells in 4% paraformaldehyde for 10 minutes at room temperature.
steps.step_rationale: Fixation preserves cellular structures and immobilizes the cells for subsequent staining procedures.
steps.span_chunk: cells were fixed in 4% paraformaldehyde for 10 min at room temperature.

steps.step_text: Wash the cells twice in PBS.
steps.step_rationale: Washing removes excess fixative and prepares cells for permeabilization.
steps.span_chunk: Cells were then washed twice in PBS

steps.step_text: Permeabilize the cells in 0.2% Triton X-100 PBS for 10 minutes at room temperature.
steps.step_rationale: Permeabilization allows antibodies to access intracellular structures.
steps.span_chunk: permeabilised in 0.2% Triton X-100 PBS for 10 min at room temperature.

steps.step_text: Block the cells in PBS with 3% BSA for 60 minutes at room temperature.
steps.step_rationale: Blocking reduces non-specific binding of antibodies to the cells.
steps.span_chunk: Blocking was performed in PBS with 3% BSA for 60 min at room temperature.

steps.step_text: Incubate the cells with Anti-Ascl1 primary antibody at 5 μg/ml final concentration in PBS with 2% FBS and 0.02% Triton X-100 overnight at 4°C without rocking.
steps.step_rationale: Primary antibody binds to the target antigen, Ascl1, present in the cells.
steps.span_chunk: Anti-Ascl1 primary antibody (Abcam, ab74065) was used at 5 μg/ml final concentration in PBS with 2% FBS and 0.02% Triton X-100 overnight at 4°C without rocking.

steps.step_text: Wash the cells 3 times in 0.02% Triton X-100 PBS for 5 minutes each.
steps.step_rationale: Washing removes unbound primary antibody.
steps.span_chunk: cells were washed 3 times in 0.02% Triton X-100 PBS for 5 mins

steps.step_text: Incubate the cells with secondary antibody (Alexa488 goat anti-rabbit IgG) diluted 1:500 in PBS with 2% FBS and 0.02% Triton X-100 for 1 hour at room temperature in the dark.
steps.step_rationale: Secondary antibody binds to the primary antibody and is conjugated with a fluorescent dye for visualization.
steps.span_chunk: incubate with secondary antibody (Alexa488 goat anti-rabbit IgG, Life Technologies) diluted 1:500 in PBS with 2% FBS and 0.02% Triton X-100 for 1 hour at room temperature in the dark.

steps.step_text: Wash the cells 3 times in 0.02% Triton X-100 PBS for 5 minutes each.
steps.step_rationale: Washing removes unbound secondary antibody.
steps.span_chunk: Cells were next washed 3 times in 0.02% Triton X-100 PBS for 5 mins

steps.step_text: Incubate the cells in DAPI (1:10,000) in PBS for 20 minutes at room temperature in the dark.
steps.step_rationale: DAPI staining labels the nuclei for visualization.
steps.span_chunk: incubated in 4′,6-diamidino-2-phenylindole (DAPI, 1:10,000) in PBS for 20 min at room temperature in the dark.

steps.step_text: Wash the cells twice in PBS.
steps.step_rationale: Final washing removes excess DAPI and prepares cells for fluorescence visualization.
steps.span_chunk: After 2 washes in PBS

steps.step_text: Visualize the fluorescence labeling with Axio Scan (Zeiss).
steps.step_rationale: Fluorescence visualization allows the observation of the labeled antigens and nuclei in the cells.
steps.span_chunk: fluorescence labelling was visualised with Axio Scan (Zeiss).

steps.step_text: Plate P19 cells into 48-well plates at the appropriate density.
steps.step_rationale: To ensure that the cells are at the correct confluence for transfection the following day.
steps.span_chunk: P19 cells were plated into 48-well plates

steps.step_text: Transfect the P19 cells the day after plating with 100 ng ΔM short-Luciferase, 50 ng pRL-TK (Renilla, Promega), and 100 ng Ascl1 using Lipofectamine 2000 in proliferation media.
steps.step_rationale: To introduce the reporter plasmids into the cells for the gene reporter assay.
steps.span_chunk: transfected the day after with 100 ng ΔM short-Luciferase (Supplementary Table S2 ), 50 ng pRL-TK (Renilla, Promega) and 100 ng Ascl1 using Lipofectamine 2000 in proliferation media

steps.step_text: Harvest one set of transfected cells the day after transfection using the Dual-Luciferase Reporter Assay System.
steps.step_rationale: To analyze the gene reporter activity in the proliferation state of the cells.
steps.span_chunk: One set of cells was harvested the day after (proliferation samples) with the Dual-Luciferase Reporter Assay System

steps.step_text: Transfer the other set of transfected cells into differentiation media and harvest them 24 hours later.
steps.step_rationale: To analyze the gene reporter activity after inducing differentiation in the cells.
steps.span_chunk: while the other set of cells was transferred into differentiation media and harvested 24 hours later

steps.step_text: Perform the luciferase assay following the manufacturer's instructions.
steps.step_rationale: To measure the luciferase activity, which reflects the activity of the reporter gene.
steps.span_chunk: Luciferase assay was performed following the manufacturer’s instructions

steps.step_text: Normalize the values for Luciferase to Renilla-Luciferase values.
steps.step_rationale: To control for transfection efficiency and cell viability, allowing for accurate comparison of reporter gene activity.
steps.span_chunk: Values for Luciferase were normalised to Renilla-Luciferase values

steps.step_text: Present the data as means ± SEM of duplicate, and repeat the experiments three times.
steps.step_rationale: To ensure the reliability and reproducibility of the experimental results.
steps.span_chunk: data are presented as means ± SEM of duplicate and experiments were repeated three times
